curated_finding: Primary study tested ponatinib in ER-positive breast cancer cells with dysregulated FGFR1 and included FGFR-driven breast models.
limitations: Cell/model evidence only; not clinical efficacy or proof that the frozen LINCS condition engaged FGFR1.

context: ERα-positive breast cancer cell models; PDGFR inhibitor and tamoxifen combination
curated_finding: PubMed abstract reports that ponatinib (alongside sunitinib) inhibited growth and induced G0-G1 arrest in ERα-positive breast cancer cell models; adding either inhibitor to tamoxifen produced more consistent growth inhibition than tamoxifen alone.
limitations: Abstract-level manual screen; exact cell-line identities and assay details require full-text review. Combination/preclinical result only; does not establish clinical efficacy or target engagement under the frozen LINCS condition.

context: ER-positive endocrine-resistant cell models (HCC-1428/LTED, MDA-MB-415/ESR1) and WHIM16 PDX; mocetinostat plus estradiol
curated_finding: The 2026 primary study reports that mocetinostat induced H3K27ac in ER-positive breast cancer models and enhanced estradiol-associated growth suppression in vitro; E2 plus mocetinostat also slowed tumor growth versus E2 alone in WHIM16 PDX. These are supplementary mocetinostat experiments alongside the paper’s main entinostat analyses.
limitations: Primary study, but mocetinostat evidence is supplementary (Fig. S1/S9); much of the paper focuses on entinostat. Preclinical endocrine-resistant models only; no clinical efficacy or ER-positive treatment indication established.

curated_finding: Primary work characterizes MK-2461 as a preferential inhibitor of activated MET and reports activity across several kinase/tumor models.
limitations: The reported models do not establish ER-positive breast-cancer-specific activity; do not infer disease linkage from MET inhibition alone.

context: MCF-7 and T47-D with estrogen and doxorubicin
curated_finding: Study found estrogen altered molecular responses to doxorubicin in ER-positive cells; low-dose co-treatment showed pro-growth signaling changes and estrogen could modify cytotoxic response.
limitations: Cell models and specific concentration/schedule; doxorubicin is a cytotoxic comparator, not a novel targeted mechanism or proof of benefit for this candidate ranking.

context: Phase Ib rebastinib plus paclitaxel or eribulin in metastatic breast cancer
curated_finding: Phase Ib trial enrolled HER2-negative metastatic breast-cancer patients and reported pharmacodynamic evidence consistent with TIE2 inhibition; HR-positive patients could be eligible, while the described individual response was in TNBC.
limitations: Combination trial; no ER-positive-specific efficacy estimate or randomized efficacy conclusion.

curated_finding: PHA-767491 was studied as a dual CDC7/CDK9 inhibitor that sensitized TNBC models to EGFR-targeted therapy.
limitations: TNBC context does not establish ER-positive disease relevance; no clinical efficacy claim.

context: Metastatic TNBC randomized phase III plus PARP mechanism re-evaluation
curated_finding: Phase III missed its prespecified coprimary OS/PFS criteria in the intention-to-treat population; separate mechanistic work disputes classification as a bona fide PARP inhibitor.
limitations: TNBC only; exploratory subgroup findings do not replace failed primary endpoints; not ER-positive evidence.

curated_finding: Focused search did not identify a compound-specific ER-positive breast-cancer study; evidence for other PPAR-gamma ligands cannot be transferred to balaglitazone.
limitations: Search was focused rather than systematic; this is an evidence gap, not proof that no such study exists.

curated_finding: Original PFI-1 study supports BET bromodomain binding/inhibition and reports leukemia-cell effects; it does not establish ER-positive breast-cancer activity.
limitations: Probe mechanism and leukemia findings are not disease-specific evidence for ER-positive breast cancer.

curated_finding: Primary study characterizes quisinostat as a potent pan-HDAC inhibitor and reports preclinical tumor-model activity outside an ER-positive-specific efficacy setting.
limitations: Broad HDAC pharmacology and other tumor models do not establish ER-positive breast-cancer efficacy.
